raw_comment:

I wonder what caused the up and down scale of weddings in the past.
The way that this relates to me and my community is, I know many people who were ready to host their wedding when Covid hit but couldn't. Lockdown was commensed and everyone had to stay in their homes.
This graph is showing the rate of weddings the past 60 years and how the recorded weddings dropped dramatically once it was the year 2020.
"Marriage or Not?"

raw_comment:
Headline: "The Rise and Fall of Weddings: Another Effect From COVID-19" 

It is abundantly clear that the pandemic has greatly impacted the wedding business, seeing as the average was around 2.3 million weddings in one year, then suddenly dropped to roughly 1.25 million in 2020. I noticed that the forecasts for the next few years increase at a surprisingly fast rate. While the situation with COVID-19 has been improving, I think that these forecasts could be extremely inaccurate due to new possible variants and the increase in cases if people become careless. I wonder what caused such a steady increase in weddings from 1975 to 1985, and what caused a steady decrease in weddings per year from 2000 to 2008. This relates to me because I know many people close to me have not been able to arrange weddings due to the shortage of venues and entertainment available.

raw_comment:
I noticed that there was a dramatic decrease in weddings during 2020. The highest number of weddings per year was a little more than 2.4 million while the lowest number of weddings per year was about 1.3 million.

I wonder how the amount of weddings were calculated. How much money does the wedding industry bring in every year? How would this graph relate to a graph of the weddings in the world?

This relates to me and my community because the wedding business boosts our economy. An increase/decrease in weddings affects the prices of venues, catering, photographers, etc as they rely on those weddings for income. 

This graph depicts the amount of weddings from 1970 and the estimated number of weddings for the next three years. A catchy headline I came up with was “They Do or They Don’t? How Has the Pandemic Affected Weddings?”.

raw_comment:
Headline: Will Weddings Still Be Safe To Continue?

I noticed that weddings have dropped immensely in the year 2020, due to the pandemic since that is the year the pandemic has most likely started around the world. Though I also noticed that the forecast shows after the year 2020, weddings will restart to increase and that leads to my wonder of how and what kind reasons led to that forecast. Possibly, there might be an assumption that the pandemic will decrease or people will start to slowly get used to the pandemic and being aware of it as they do weddings, instead of just not doing any weddings like when the pandemic started. Though another question is why the graph predicts the wedding to decrease back again after it restarted to increase. Possibly people might start doing weddings or delayed weddings after the pandemic lessens, then there would be fewer weddings once a large amount of people finishes it all at once. This relates to my community since I do know a few people around me who had trouble arranging weddings or delays due to the pandemic. This graph shows all throughout the past years until the present and the future which reminds us once again how much of a big impact the pandemic has on our community and daily lives.

I notice that the number of people getting married increased until around 1995 when it started slowly decreasing. There was then a massive decrease in 2020 (when covid started). The numbers then started to increase and the prediction is that they will continue to increase and then decrease.

I wonder why there is a slow decrease over time.

I notice that the amount of money spent on weddings from the 1970s to the 2010s is mostly around 2.1 million to 2.4 million but in 2020, the number drops drastically to around 1.2 million. I also notice that instead of having a lot of points, the graph looks like a step graph and stays constant throughout each year. 

I wonder if the amount spent drastically drops because people are just not having as many weddings because of covid or if it is because of the limitations and things like not many people can come so the wedding has to be smaller. I wonder why it is predicted that the number of weddings will go up a lot from the normal predicted. Is it because a lot of weddings have been pushed back and are going to be when quarantine ends? 

This relates to me and my community because weddings are a big point in many peoples lives and a lot of things have been pushed back due to covid, including weddings.

"Wedding Plans have been Wetted Down"

raw_comment:
Title: Matrimony Madness
I notice that the graph shows the number of weddings per year (each line increasing by .2 million) along with the year that the weddings take place (increasing in 5-year increments). I also notice that the graph begins with a small rise between 1970-1975 and a more steady rise between 1975 and 1985. Along with those increases, there is also a slow decrease going into 2010 and then a significant drop in 2020, when the pandemic hit. The drop occurred in the peak of COVID-19, and then going further into 2021/2022 has begun to rise back up, almost reaching the pre-pandemic numbers by .2 million or so. During the pandemic, people either decided to wait or postpone most weddings for the safety of themselves & their families. As more things begin to open up and vaccination becomes more widely available, people have begun feeling more comfortable holding the gatherings. The last thing I notice is that the forecast is that in 2023 or so, the number of weddings will greatly increase reaching the point of pre-pandemic numbers. I wonder if the predicted numbers will be accurate, or if the new variants will cause the number of weddings to decrease again. I also wonder why there was a decrease in weddings around the years 1975 & 2010, and if they were just due to the ages around and wanting to get married at that time. The last thing I wonder is what happened to the wedding industry during the pandemic, and how they are readjusting now that things are more normal.

raw_comment:
On this graph about weddings in the U.S. by each year, I notice a lot of different things. 

Some of the things that stand out the most include:

1. The number of mar weddings taking place declines in 2020. I assume this is because people were not out meeting each other or gathering together due to Coronavirus. This would be the root of why weddings were not being planned.

2. It seems that in the years to come more weddings will occur. Now, I guess that this will be primarily due to people being vaccinated and feeling more comfortable about gathering for large events such as a wedding.

Something else I know that impacted this graph slightly was that in 2015, gay marriage was legalized which explains the small rise in marriages. 

Also, from 1975-1985 there was an increase which I would predict was from the ending of the Vietnam War. And, a decrease happened during the early 2000s which I would predict was due to 9/11.

I wonder why there will be another slight decrease in 2022.

A good title may be: Wedding Wars: Coronavirus vs. U.S. Marriages

raw_comment: This graph describes the trend in the number of weddings every five years since 1970.  From 1970 to 2019 there was a pretty steady number of weddings each year. raw_comment: I noticed that the wedding business between the time period 1970-2015 increased in number and this number was between 2.1 million to 2.5 million. However, during 2020 weddings in the United States decreased massively in number due to the pandemic. I wonder why the graph depicts that in the next coming years, the number of weddings in the United States will rise. In my community, there is not a lot of people at wedding gatherings because they fear they will be affected by the virus. This has led to invitations being limited. Personally, I had a youth leader who wanted to get married at the beginning of 2020 but due to the pandemic, he had to postpone his wedding to 2021. A headline I would have given this graph is: "COVID: The wedding desert".

raw_comment:
"The COVID Spreadings to end the Weddings"

We notice how prior to 2020, there were consistently around 2.1-2.5 million weddings each year. In 2020, we notice that number drop by over 1 million to the year prior plateauing at around 1.3 million weddings. We wonder slightly how it spiked back up to 2+ million in just two years or so even while still in the midst of the pandemic happening. This does show however how eager people were to get back into having weddings after the prior limit of social gatherings and how it impacted so many plans for so many people over the course of the past year losing out on opportunities for not only the future married couples but the wedding industry itself.

Does swiping right lead to increased “I do’s”?

raw_comment:
Thanks to all the students who responded.   Here are some of the catchy headlines that we received:  "Something Borrowed, Something Blue, A Predicted Surge In Weddings Is New" by Maggie of Academy of Saint Elizabeth of Morristown, New Jersey; "Covid Ruined Weddings” by Ms. Mitchell’s 5th grade class in Mississauga, Ontario; “Will Weddings Be Up and Running Post-Covid?” by Evangeline of Concord, New Hampshire, “The Great Depression of Wedding Businesses,” by Cynthia in Pennsylvania; and “2020: The Year Weddings Took a Break” by Gabriella and “Is Love Dead or is Covid Alive?” by Paige, both from Gilbert, Arizona.
 
You can continue to post responses.  Please check back by Friday, Feb. 18 to see the Reveal with a link to the original New York Times article, some questions about the graph, and a few Stat Nuggets.
 
Please visit our archive to see all graphs in this series (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphs).
View our archives that link to all past releases, organized by topic (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphsTopicIndex), 
graph type (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphsTypeIndex) and 
Stat Nugget (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphsStatNuggetsIndex). 
 
Signing off – Sharon Hessney of Boston, who went to many weddings in the summer of 2021 that were postponed from 2020, and Kristina Barnaby of Fairfield, Connecticut, whose friends were happily – and safely – married before the pandemic hit.

raw_comment:
In this graph, I notice a drastic decrease in weddings in the year 2020. However, about 1 or 2 years later the graph increases a little but then starts to decrease again slowly. I wonder if the drastic decrease in the wedding business was affected by the coronavirus and if so, I wonder if people ended up postponing their wedding or did they just completely give up. I also wonder why the graph predicts the wedding business to continue to decrease as it is only 2022 and has not yet reached 2025. This relates to my community because I know many of my family friends who have planned weddings in 2020 but were postponed due to the virus. This graph shows the annual number of weddings from 1970 is shown until the predicted number of weddings in 2025.
 
“The Great Depression of Wedding Businesses”

So, in order to account for the years in between, they did a step graph which is easier to deduct from compared to a line graph. Is marriage in general just not important to people anymore? This relates to me and my community because less and less people in my life have gotten married.

raw_comment:
In this graph we noticed that there is an extreme drop in weddings near 2020, which we can only assume is due to COVID-19. Though, it is very surprising that even with the huge drop, there will still around 1.2 million weddings, as most of the world was to be in lockdown. We also noticed that there is quite a bit of regular fluctuation. The graph does not seem to be very linear in the increases or decreases.

raw_comment: In this graph, I immediately noticed that wedding numbers dropped rapidly in 2020. This is most likely due to the quarantine months due to COVID-19 when people were not allowed to hold public events and had to postpone their weddings. Right after, wedding numbers increased in the years 2021-2022, resulting from the lessening of quarantine rules. I wonder why wedding rates went the lowest in years around 2007-2010. My guess could be that it relates to the economic recession in 2008 that caused many people to lose jobs and money. Without money, people most likely weren't able to afford to host weddings. The same thing happened around 1975 as well which also makes me wonder what the causes were. This graph relates to me and my community because I know people personally had their weddings postponed due to COVID-19. A title that summarizes the data in this graph is, "Wedding Growth Throughout the Years."

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
The first and most obvious thing I notice is the dramatic decrease in weddings in 2020. Having lived through that time, I can firmly assert that this is because of the pandemic, COVID. From my own experience, I know of many people who postponed their wedding in order to have an actual ceremony with the people whom they want to be there. I also notice what appears to be a steady trend in increase and decrease. The curve of the graph almost looks like a sine curve, and none of the statistics appear to be alarming or out of the ordinary before 2020. 
What do you wonder?
I wonder how they predicted the graph up until 2025. Is this prediction going to be accurate? I understand why they forecasted a surge in weddings because many people were waiting until they could have a large wedding, but how did they predict the rest of the graph?
How does this relate to you and your community?
This relates to my community and me for I did have to live through the dramatic decrease in weddings. We were all quarantined inside during the year 2020, and it was sad to see so many happy people have to lose money on their wedding deposits and have to wait to have the wedding they wanted. 
What's going on in this graph?
"Did COVID take the love away?"

raw_comment:
The amount of weddings?  Or, the number of weddings?  What's the difference?

When we can count things, like weddings, we use the word "number."  Example:  The number of weddings is now rebounding.

When we can't count things, like love, we use the word "amount."  Example:  The amount of love has not changed.  

Good to know!

raw_comment:
I noticed that the number of weddings in the US generally hovered between 2.1 to 2.5 million per year from 1970 up until 2019. Fluctuations, in the numbers align with major events at the time such as the 1973-75 recession and the 2008 financial crisis. However, in 2020, there is a drastic drop in the number of weddings held that year due to the cancellation and postponement of wedding plans in accordance with COVID safety protocols. Perhaps a cause could even be the pandemic preventing people from meeting and developing their relationships. The number of weddings begins to climb the year after and spikes to all-time highs in the next 2 years due to the number of people unable to hold their weddings in 2020.

I mainly find myself curious in the quick resumption of weddings after 2020, as COVID was still going strong then and was and is a persisting problem. Lastly, I find myself curious in the reasoning behind the predicted decrease in weddings from 2023-25 and onwards.

This relates to me and my community because I think people are all aware of the obstacles the pandemic posed, especially in its first year, toward weddings, but it's shocking seeing its extent and the spike in weddings afterward seeing with a graph and numbers. People have had to cancel weddings and make sacrifices in their size in 2020 and years since.

If June is the best wedding month, is the post-onset pandemic the new ideal wedding time? The trends and patterns leading up to this reality.

raw_comment:
Impacts of COVID on Weddings

I'm noticing that there had been a drastic decline in weddings in 2020, dropping from around 2.2 million to 1.4 million. This was probably due to strict COVID regulations as well as the lockdowns that restricted people from gatherings. It's interesting that in all other years, wedding numbers have generally been consistent with no other significant changes from year to year. I'm wondering why wedding numbers were a bit lower in 1975 and around 2010. In addition, I find it interesting that forecasts are saying that numbers should dip in 2025. This makes sense as there will most likely be another wave of the virus, but I was also thinking that couples who may have held off their weddings in the last two years would want to hold them in the next few years too. This graph relates back to me because I know of a couple family friends that have postponed their wedding because of the pandemic. This data can also reflect the statutes of other large events/gatherings such as graduation ceremonies or birthday parties.

raw_comment:
I notice that the rate at which couples are getting married in the United States remained at approximately 2.3 million weddings throughout the entire late twentieth century. However the weddings per year begin to slowly decrease in the twenty first century and drastically plummet in 2020. The projected amount of weddings in the next few years is expected to skyrocket. 
I wonder how other historical events affected the number of weddings annually in the past. Did tragedies such as World War II have a similar fact on weddings as Covid did 2020?
This relates to the world including myself as many important events in the world had to be rescheduled to limit the spread of this disease. 
Title: Weddings Postponed: COVID’s Effect on Love

raw_comment:
In this graph, I noticed that the number of weddings during the pandemic dropped by about 1 million. This is probably due to both lockdowns closing wedding facilities, capacity restrictions on large events, and maybe fewer people meeting each other in general since we were stuck in our homes. 

I wonder why the marriages were the highest in 1980s but there was a drop in the number of marriages in 2008. After some outside research, I discovered that there was a major financial crisis in 2007-2008 that could affect the welfare of many people. A good economy means more marriages.

This relates to me because personally, I have a cousin who was unable to get married during the pandemic because of restrictions and shutdowns. Luckily, she is married now and she most likely contributed to the large spike in marriages following the pandemic.

Title: Love is in the Air: The Wedding Business is Coming Back Strong!

raw_comment:
I noticed that the number of weddings in the United States plummeted in the year 2020. In a few years, the number of weddings rose from 1.3 million to 2.5. Many weddings were postponed due to the rise in Covid cases however, it still seems like a very rapid increase. 
I wonder why there are flatlines in the data. What does that mean? Even though we are still experiencing surges in cases, the number of weddings is still increasing. According to the graph, it seems like the peek will begin to decrease within a year or so, but what is causing this? I would be interested to see a graph explaining the number of people in attendance at each wedding as opposed to the number of weddings themselves. Even with the rise in the number of weddings, are people throwing large or small weddings?  
This relates to my community since many people are hosting weddings that have fewer people. I attended a wedding last summer that had 50% fewer people due to Covid. Many out-of-state and elderly family members did not attend as well. It definitely changed the demographic of weddings.

Title Idea: Weddings During A Pandemic?
I've noticed that once COVID-19 hit in 2020 there were not as many weddings. This is because of the Pandemic and everything got shut down. People were supposed to stay in there homes unless they went grocery shopping or were doing something outside (like biking, walking, running etc) I know many people who had to post - pone their weddings because of Covid-19, or had very small ones. I think the reason people started having weddings again is because we have learned more about COVID-19. We now have a vaccine, and I think this really has helped a lot. I think a lot of weddings have a requirment for a COVID-19 vaccine, and maybe a mask mandate depending on if it's inside or outside. Now that we know more about COVID-19 I think this is why people are beginning to feel safer to do things with people. Get vaccinated and wear your mask!

raw_comment:
Notice: I noticed that the number of weddings per year dropped by around 1 million during 2020/the pandemic. I also noticed that the number of weddings had already been decreasing/flucutating slowly for many years since its peak in the 1980s, however, the 2020 drop was the most drastic.

Wonder: I wonder why the forecast doesn't predict that after the pandemic the number of weddings will shoot up even more than predicted. In my mind, all the people who didn't have weddings would plan theirs to be as soon as possible and the total number would be much higher than predicted.

Relate: This relates to me and my community because I was supposed to go to a wedding this year, but it got rescheduled due to COVID-19 and the new variants. 

Title: Wedding Business: How long will it rest?

raw_comment:
What I notice:
- There was a huge drop in weddings in 2020, which was when COVID came
- 1980-2017, weddings stayed pretty consistent, over 2 million each year
- Marriages from 2023+ is forecasted to increase signifcantly and then return to it’s normal trend before the pandemic

What I wonder:
* Why is marriages forecasted to increase significantly in the coming years?
* Will the number of marriages increase because of rise in population, immigration, or because people couldn’t have weddings during the pandemic?
* Marriagres dropped really low in 2020 but then also made a significant comeback (not as much as the years before though). I wonder if that was because people was not as cautious or because there was a rise in population? Why did it suddenly come back up after 2020?

A headline could be: Trend of Marriages Over the Years

raw_comment:
I noticed that since COVID was responsible for canceling the majority of weddings in 2020, the time period immediately after has seen a major increase in the number of weddings. However, I also notice that after this increase, they are predicting it to drop to the lower side of the average weddings per year.

I wonder why they are predicting another decrease in the number of weddings. Does it have to do with COVID and the prediction of another outbreak? Or, is it because people were not able to meet others during the lockdown and possibly they are expecting a decrease due to the average time period of dating before marriage lining up with when quarantine began? 

I personally had two family members' weddings that were pushed back due to COVID. They both occurred over this past summer, showing the major increase in real life.

raw_comment:
Title: "Here is the Zoom Link to Our Wedding"

What do you notice?
I notice immediately that 2020 is an outlier. This is most likely due to the pandemic and the CDC's decision to limit social gatherings in order to prevent the spread of the Covid-19 virus. The graph stays fairly consistent in the years prior to 2020. Between 2020 and 2025, the wedding forecasts seem to work their way back up the normal average of weddings in the United States by year, which seems to be about 2.2-2.4 million. This is most likely a direct result of the mask-wearing protocols as well as the vaccination distributions. 

What do you wonder?
I wonder why there was a peak of weddings in the United States in the year 1985. When I think of the eighties, I think of bright, flashy lights and unique hairstyles. I wonder if people from this decade had more weddings because it seemed more dramatized and fun. 

How does this relate to you and your community?
This relates to me and my community because we are directly impacted by this Pandemic. We are living in an outlier time where we may first-handedly experience events like online weddings, masked weddings, etc.

1. What do you notice?
I noticed that COVID has dramatically affected the number of weddings in the United States. I also noticed that it is predicted that the number of weddings will increase and make up for the weddings that were canceled due to the pandemic. 
2. What do you wonder?
I wonder how much money people lost if they had to reschedule their wedding. I also wonder what the average number of people to attend a wedding is and how much this affected many different industries. I also wonder if this is slowing down the amount of people getting engaged. 
3. What impact does this have on you and your community?
This impacts me and my community because I have family friends that were supposed to get married but since COVID happened, their wedding got canceled and they had to make their guest list even shorter than planned so not as many people could come and celebrate. As well as this, this means that if I were to attend a wedding, this probably means that I would have to pay even more money because there has been an inflation in prices on goods and services.

In this graph, we see the years 1970-2025 that display the number of weddings held in the United States. A catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea would be “Will you be able to reschedule your wedding?”
